::: {.why}
You already refuse to split relatives across folds of a genetic prediction study; overlapping forward returns are the same dependence structure, and standard cross-validation walks straight into it.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State precisely which assumption overlapping labels violate and what it does to a cross-validated performance estimate.
- Demonstrate the inflation with a synthetic experiment where the true relationship is zero.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build the demonstration: generate features with no relationship at all to forward returns, construct 10-day overlapping labels, and run standard 5-fold cross-validation. The cross-validated R-squared will be positive and it will look significant. Report it, then repeat with non-overlapping labels and show it collapses.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Write the mechanism out: adjacent observations share most of their label, so a fold boundary places nearly identical observations on both sides, and the model is scored partly on data it trained on. Name the analogous situation in your own field and note that the correction there is the same one you will build tomorrow.
:::
:::
